meta.name: Salesforce Certified AI Associate
meta.notes: Initial Salesforce AI Associate pack — covers the four exam domains: AI Fundamentals (predictive vs generative, supervised/unsupervised, NLP), AI Capabilities in CRM (Einstein features), Ethical Considerations (Salesforce Trusted AI Principles, bias, hallucinations, Einstein Trust Layer, human-in-the-loop), and Data for AI (data quality dimensions, Data Cloud harmonization, RAG grounding). Correct-position spread across A/B/C/D.

questions.question: A marketing team wants a system that writes first-draft product-launch emails from a short brief, while the sales team wants a system that scores existing leads by likelihood to convert. Which pair of AI types matches these two needs, in order?
options: Predictive AI for the marketing draft, and generative AI for the lead score
Reinforcement learning for both, tuned with different reward signals
Generative AI for the marketing draft, and predictive AI for the lead score
Rule-based expert systems for both, since neither task uses training data
questions.explanation: Generative AI produces new content (text, images, code) from a prompt, so it fits the email-drafting task; predictive AI uses historical labelled data to output a probability or a class, which is exactly what lead scoring needs. Option A inverts the two — predictive models classify rather than write prose, and generative models produce content rather than a calibrated conversion score. Reinforcement learning is trained by reward signals during interaction (game agents, robotics) and is a poor fit for a one-shot email draft or a batch lead-scoring model. Rule-based expert systems can encode explicit heuristics but cannot write fluent prose or generalise from thousands of historical opportunities the way modern predictive models do.

questions.question: Salesforce publishes five Trusted AI Principles that guide how Einstein features are designed. Which set correctly lists all five?
options: Responsible, Accountable, Transparent, Empowering, Inclusive
Fair, Secure, Explainable, Auditable, Private
Trusted, Fast, Personal, Connected, Intelligent
Bias-free, Copyright-safe, Consent-based, Grounded, Human-supervised
questions.explanation: Salesforce's Trusted AI Principles are Responsible, Accountable, Transparent, Empowering, and Inclusive — memorise them because the exam tests the exact wording, not synonyms. Option B lists common AI-governance ideas but is not the Salesforce framework. Option C is a Salesforce marketing pillar list for the Customer 360 platform, not the AI principles. Option D describes practical safeguards (some of which the Einstein Trust Layer implements), but they are not the named principles.

questions.question: An admin audits the Lead object and finds that 40% of records still list phone numbers and job titles that were correct three years ago but have not been updated since. Which data-quality dimension is primarily failing here?
options: Completeness — required fields are populated but with stale values
Consistency — the same field disagrees across related records
Uniqueness — the same lead is stored more than once
Age — the values were correct once but have become out of date
questions.explanation: Age (sometimes called recency or timeliness) measures how current the data is; records that were accurate when captured but have not been refreshed fail on age even when every field is filled in. Completeness would be the answer if fields were blank — here they are populated, just stale. Consistency addresses conflicts across systems (e.g. phone number differs between Lead and Contact), which is a different failure mode. Uniqueness targets duplicate records rather than out-of-date values.

questions.question: A bank trains a loan-approval model on historical decisions in which one demographic group was systematically denied loans. Deployed as-is, the model reproduces the same pattern. Which type of bias is most directly responsible?
options: Automation bias — humans over-trust the model's output during review
Historical (or societal) bias — the training data itself encodes past inequity
Confirmation bias — the modeller only looked for evidence supporting the design
Sampling bias caused by an undersized validation set
questions.explanation: Historical bias arises when the training data reflects an unfair pattern that existed in the real world; the model has no incentive to correct it and will faithfully reproduce the discrimination. Automation bias describes how humans behave around a model's output, not why the model itself is biased. Confirmation bias is about the modeller's reasoning process rather than the input data. Sampling bias is a real problem, but a small validation set typically causes high variance, not a systematic demographic skew — the loan-history skew is baked into the training data itself.

questions.question: A service manager wants to use Einstein-powered generative replies but is worried that customer PII typed into cases will leave the Salesforce trust boundary when prompts are sent to the large language model. Which capability of the Einstein Trust Layer most directly addresses this concern?
options: Prompt Builder templates, which restrict which merge fields authors can insert
The Trust Layer's audit trail, which records every prompt and response for compliance review
Dynamic data masking, which replaces sensitive fields with placeholders before the prompt is sent and rehydrates them in the response
Zero-retention agreements with model providers, which guarantee prompts are not stored after inference
questions.explanation: Dynamic data masking is the Einstein Trust Layer feature that detects PII in the prompt, swaps it for placeholders before the request leaves the Salesforce trust boundary, and rehydrates the real values in the response — so the model provider never sees the raw personal data. Prompt Builder templates limit what an author can compose but do not mask PII already in a chosen field. The audit trail is a governance capability for after-the-fact review; it does not prevent PII from leaving. Zero-retention agreements stop providers from persisting prompts, which is important but does not stop the raw PII from being transmitted in the first place — masking does.

questions.question: A sales operations lead wants Salesforce to score each open opportunity from 1 to 99 for likelihood to close, using patterns learned from historical won and lost deals. Which Einstein capability fits this need most directly?
options: Einstein Opportunity Scoring, which produces a per-opportunity likelihood score from historical outcomes
Einstein Bots, which automate deflection of case volume from the service team
Einstein Search, which personalises which records appear at the top of a search
Einstein Copilot, which answers natural-language questions about CRM data
questions.explanation: Einstein Opportunity Scoring is the standard Sales Cloud feature that trains on the org's own Closed Won/Closed Lost history and returns a numeric likelihood score per open opportunity — exactly the ask. Einstein Bots handle service-channel automation. Einstein Search improves relevance ranking of the global search bar. Einstein Copilot is a conversational assistant; it can summarise or discuss records but is not the feature that produces the calibrated close-probability score across the pipeline.

questions.question: An organisation has customer records in Marketing Cloud, Service Cloud, an ERP, and a data warehouse. Before it can use that data to ground a generative AI assistant, Data Cloud needs to reconcile the various customer identifiers into a single unified profile. What is this reconciliation step called?
options: Ingestion — bringing raw records into Data Cloud through connectors
Segmentation — splitting the unified population into audiences for activation
Activation — publishing a segment back to a downstream engagement system
Identity resolution and harmonization — mapping source records to a canonical customer profile
questions.explanation: Harmonization maps disparate source fields to a common data model, and identity resolution matches records that refer to the same real-world person, producing the Unified Individual profile that grounding queries can trust. Ingestion is the earlier step of getting raw records into Data Cloud through streams or connectors. Segmentation happens after unification and slices the audience for a use case. Activation is the last step, pushing a segment out to Marketing Cloud or another engagement channel.

questions.question: A data scientist trains a model to classify support cases as billing, technical, or account by learning from 50,000 cases that human agents have already tagged. Which category of machine learning does this workflow belong to?
options: Unsupervised learning, because the model discovers the three categories on its own
Supervised learning, because each training example is paired with a known correct label
Reinforcement learning, because the model earns a reward for each correct classification during training
Generative modelling, because the model outputs new synthetic support cases
questions.explanation: Supervised learning is defined by training on labelled examples — each input paired with the known correct output — which is precisely what the 50,000 human-tagged cases provide. Unsupervised learning discovers structure without labels (clustering, anomaly detection); here the labels already exist. Reinforcement learning trains an agent through reward feedback in an environment, which is not how a batch classifier is fit. Generative modelling produces new samples that resemble the training distribution — a different objective from tagging existing cases.

questions.question: A healthcare company plans to use an AI assistant to help triage nurses prioritise incoming patient calls. What is the best-practice pattern for deploying AI in a decision that carries clinical risk?
options: Deploy the model fully autonomously so response times are minimised, with a monthly audit
Show the AI recommendation only after the nurse commits their own decision, to prevent anchoring
Keep a qualified human in the loop who reviews and can override every AI recommendation before it takes effect
Restrict the model to summarising the call transcript and forbid any recommendation output
questions.explanation: Human-in-the-loop is the Salesforce-recommended and industry-standard pattern for high-stakes AI: the model surfaces a recommendation, but a qualified human reviews, can override, and remains accountable for the outcome — this operationalises the Accountable and Empowering Trusted AI principles. Full autonomy is inappropriate when errors can harm patients and violates accountability. Hiding the recommendation until after the human decides defeats the productivity purpose of the assistant. Restricting the model to pure summarisation gives up useful decision support and still leaves the summary itself unreviewed for hallucinations.

questions.question: A generative AI assistant confidently returns a plausible but fabricated policy number when asked about a customer's contract. What is this failure mode called, and which mitigation technique most directly reduces it?
options: Overfitting, mitigated by adding regularisation to the training loop
Prompt injection, mitigated by input sanitisation on the user's message
Model drift, mitigated by scheduled retraining on newer data
Hallucination, mitigated by retrieval-augmented generation that grounds the answer in the customer's actual CRM records
questions.explanation: A hallucination is when a large language model produces fluent, confident output that is not supported by any real source — the fabricated policy number is a textbook example. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) mitigates this by fetching authoritative records (in Salesforce, from Data Cloud or CRM objects) and injecting them into the prompt as grounding, so the model has real facts to cite instead of inventing them. Overfitting refers to a model that memorises its training set and fails to generalise — a different pathology. Prompt injection is an adversarial attack where a user embeds hidden instructions in their message. Model drift is a gradual degradation as the world changes underneath a static model; retraining helps drift but does not stop a well-calibrated model from inventing missing facts.
